svg.title: Queue amplification at the knee
svg.desc: Three boxes linked by arrows: every step 2% longer, so capacity is 2% lower; each burst of arrivals drains later, so the next burst finds a queue; the queue's waits add up in the tail of TTFT. Below, two panels from the simulator at 4 requests per second on one trace, with every step 2% faster, as priced, and 2% slower. Left: the requests queued for a seat or prefilling over the 70-second run; the three lines rise and fall together with the bursts, the slower steps highest, peaking at 16 waiting requests against 11 for the faster ones. Right: every request's TTFT, sorted; the curves agree for the fastest fifth of requests and spread apart above it, with p95 values of 2.4, 3.1 and 3.9 seconds.
svg.text: Queue amplification at the knee: 4 requests per second
The same 240 arrivals, Qwen3-8B on one RTX A6000, 1024 tokens in, 128 out. Only the price of every step changes.
